<issue>
hugo convert does not copy "non content file" files if --output is set
Hi all,

I probably found another issue concerning _page resources:_

`hugo convert` deletes all page resources if the flag `output` is set, e. g.:

```
hugo convert toTOML --output converted
```

With the `unsafe` flag set everything works as expected:

```
hugo convert toTOML --unsafe
```

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Hugo), find the code for `hugo convert` command (commands/convert.go). Print the full relevant code of convert/convertContents/ writeContentToFile, showing how --output is handled and how files are written.

content.content: {"summary":"There is no `writeContentToFile` function anywhere in the repo (grep finds nothing). The file-writing logic lives in `convertAndSavePage`, which calls `helpers.WriteToDisk`. `--output` is handled in `convertAndSavePage` (commands/convert.go:188-192). `convertContents` (line 203) only guards against running without `--output` unless `--unsafe` is set. Nothing was modified.","findings":["commands/convert.go:113: `--output/-o` is registered as persistent flag `outputDir` (default \"\"), with `--unsafe` as a bool flag at the same level.","commands/convert.go:203-206 (convertContents): if c.outputDir == \"\" && !c.unsafe, it returns newUserError(\"Unsafe operation not allowed, use --unsafe or set a different output path\"). Otherwise it calls c.h.Build(hugolib.BuildCfg{SkipRender: true}), takes site := c.h.Sites[0], and loops over site.AllPages() calling convertAndSavePage(p, site, format).","commands/convert.go:186-193 (convertAndSavePage): newFilename := p.File().Filename(). If c.outputDir != \"\", contentDir = filepath.Base(strings.TrimSuffix(newFilename, p.File().Path())) and newFilename = filepath.Join(c.outputDir, contentDir, p.File().Path()). So with --output the file goes under <output>/<content-section-dir>/<path>; without --unsafe, it overwrites the source file in place.","commands/convert.go:195-197: fs := hugofs.Os; if err := helpers.WriteToDisk(newFilename, &newContent, fs); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf(\"failed to save file %q:: %w\", newFilename, err) }.","helpers/path.go:245-247: `func WriteToDisk(inpath string, r io.Reader, fs afero.Fs) error { return afero.WriteReader(fs, inpath, r) }`. afero.WriteReader creates the file and copies the reader; it does not create parent directories itself beyond what afero does.","commands/convert.go:133-186 (convertAndSavePage) first recurses into page bundle resources of type \"page\", skips pages with nil File(), parses front matter with pageparser.ParseFrontMatterAndContent, converts time.Time values to RFC3339 for JSON/YAML/TOML, and renders the new front matter via parser.InterfaceToFrontMatter into newContent before appending pf.Content.","Possible bug at commands/convert.go:140-143: on file Open error it calls file.Close() on a nil handle and then returns nil, which would panic or silently skip."],"confidence":0.85}

input.instruction: In /testbed (Hugo), for a page.Page's p.Resources() items of non-"page" type (e.g. images/text), how can I get the source file path/filesystem metadata (e.g. fileInfo / Meta().Filename / Open)? Check resources/resource.go, resources/resource_spec.go, resources/page, resource/ interfaces (e.g. resource.Source, fileInfo providers, hugofs.FileMetaInfo). Report exact interface names and method signatures usable from package commands without modifying code.

content.content: {"summary":"Non-page resources returned by p.Resources() are concrete *resources.genericResource (or resourceAdapter for transforms). Their source path (sourcePath) is unexported, and no exported method exposes hugofs.FileMetaInfo or Meta().Filename. The only exported route to source bytes is ReadSeekCloser(), reachable from other packages via an anonymous interface assertion. resource.Source only has Publish(), so it gives no path or file info.","findings":["resources/resource/resourcetypes.go:72 `type Resource interface { ResourceWithoutMeta; ResourceMetaProvider }`; ResourceMetaProvider (line 110) gives Name(), Params; no Open, path or Meta method is exported on the public Resource interface.","resources/resource/resources.go:257 `type Source interface { Publish() error }`; this does not expose the source path or file info.","resources/resource.go:397 `func (l *genericResource) ReadSeekCloser() (hugio.ReadSeekCloser, error)` is the exported way to read source bytes; it delegates to sd.OpenReadSeekCloser (line 398). Usable from commands via `r.(interface{ ReadSeekCloser() (hugio.ReadSeekCloser, error) })`.","resources/resource.go:478 `func (l *genericResource) sourcePath() string` is unexported (returns sd.SourceFilenameOrPath), so commands cannot call it directly. Its interface sourcePathProvider is at resources/resource.go:743 and is also unexported.","resources/resource.go:245 and 301-307: the internal baseResourceInternal and fileInfo interfaces (setOpenSource, size, hash, etc.) are unexported; they are not usable from package commands.","resources/resource.go:88 `SourceFilenameOrPath string // Used for error logging.` is a field in the unexported source descriptor, so it is not reachable from commands.","hugofs/fileinfo.go:159 `type FileMetaInfo interface { fs.DirEntry; MetaProvider; FileInfoOptionals }`, with MetaProvider at line 167 `Meta() *FileMeta`. FileMeta (line 66) has exported fields PathInfo *paths.Path and Filename string, plus OpenFunc (line 87). These are exported but are only reachable if a resource exposes a FileMetaInfo, and no resource method returns one (resources/page/page_nop.go:154 and testhelpers_test.go:199 are page-level FileInfo(), not resource-level).","common/hugio/readers.go:135 `type OpenReadSeekCloser func() (ReadSeekCloser, error)`; common/hugio/readers.go:61 `type ReadSeekCloserProvider interface { ReadSeekCloser() (ReadSeekCloser, error) }`. These are exported and match the ReadSeekCloser method above.","Practical answer: from package commands you can read bytes with a type assertion to `interface{ ReadSeekCloser() (hugio.ReadSeekCloser, error) }`, but you cannot get the file path or FileMeta without changing code. Hugo's own file metadata lives on the hugofs side, so you would need to map from the page's source path via p.File() (page-level, not checked here) or the content dir."],"confidence":0.7}
